nodes.name: Capture Webhook
nodes.notes: POST only, and the path is the workflow id spelled out rather than left to the node id n8n mints, so the production URL is one a client can be configured with before this file has ever reached an instance. Response mode onReceived, so the request is answered as it lands and the pass runs behind it: the alternative holds the socket open through extraction, the findings write and the invocation of ar-score, none of which a capture client asked about. authentication is written none rather than left off, because a default nobody wrote down is a decision nobody reviewed; what stands in front of this path is whatever fronts the instance, and this canvas judges shape rather than caller. typeVersion 2 is what the other nodes here are held to as well: nothing in this repository validates an n8n parameter name or version, no n8n package being installed, so these four are reviewed rather than checked.

parameters.query:
WITH envelope AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS posted
),
claim AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN e.posted ->> 'sourceId' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
      THEN (e.posted ->> 'sourceId')::bigint
    END AS source_id
  FROM envelope e
),
source AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.domain_id,
    s.kind,
    s.endpoint,
    s.parser_config,
    s.contract,
    s.consecutive_failures,
    s.last_success_at,
    s.last_failure_at,
    s.enabled,
    s.flagged
  FROM sources s
  WHERE s.id = (SELECT source_id FROM claim)
)
-- The first node after the trigger, and the shape the parent design fixes for every
-- workflow in this set (.specs/2026-08-19-research-pipeline-port.md, section 4): the
-- domain's personas and taxonomy, read as ONE query answering exactly one row. Both
-- halves are argued in full on ar-ingest's Load Domain Context, which asks the same
-- question of the same tables and is not repeated here. What is written out below is
-- the half that differs, which is how this canvas gets a domain at all.

-- Nothing has named one. ar-ingest is invoked with a run id and reads its domain back
-- off that row, an id the dispatcher wrote. All this trigger carries is a POST body
-- from a stranger, and no part of it has been judged: capture-contract.ts runs two
-- node groups below, after the raw body has been stored. So the domain is resolved
-- through the source the envelope CLAIMS, and this statement is where the claim is
-- read.

-- The whole posted body binds as ONE jsonb parameter rather than one parameter per
-- member. A body may be a bare string, a number or a list as readily as an object,
-- JSON.stringify makes every one of those a valid jsonb literal, and the members are
-- then read where a comment can say what each one is instead of inside an expression
-- no gate reads. The nullif is the other half of that: JSON.stringify(null) binds the
-- JSON null literal rather than SQL NULL, so a request with no body at all would
-- otherwise arrive here as a value.

-- ->> answers NULL for every jsonb that is not an object, measured on this schema for
-- a string, a number, a list and the null literal, so a body that is not an object
-- needs no guard in front of the read: the pattern test is handed NULL, the CASE
-- answers NULL, and nothing raises over a shape somebody else chose.

-- The digit bound is {1,18} rather than +, and the difference between them is a
-- raise. A longer run of digits matches + and then overflows the bigint cast, which
-- is an error this node could not survive; eighteen digits sits inside bigint's
-- nineteen, and no sources id is going to reach it.

-- Three readings come out of this row and they are not two. A null source_id means
-- the envelope named no source this statement could read. A source_id with a null
-- domain_id means it named one that matches no sources row. A domain_id means the
-- capture resolved, and an empty list beside it is a domain that states no personas,
-- no categories, no terms or no criteria. Read them in that order: a length says
-- nothing until both ids have been read.

-- Nothing here refuses, which is the rule capture-contract.ts states from the other
-- side. The raw body is stored before anything judges it, so a node turning an
-- unreadable source id away HERE would lose the capture at exactly the point that
-- ordering exists to protect. What this answers instead is a row saying what it could
-- and could not resolve. One thing the group below cannot do with it is store a
-- document under a null domain: documents.domain_id is NOT NULL, so a capture naming
-- a source this database does not hold has no row to be written to, and what that
-- pass records is that group's to decide.

-- The source row is fetched here rather than by a lookup node below because this is
-- where it is read anyway: the domain is reached THROUGH it, so the round trip is
-- already spent and a second node would be a second branch to reason about. to_jsonb
-- over the CTE is what projects it, so the member list is declared once, in the CTE
-- above, and a column added there travels with no second edit. This node acts on none
-- of them: enabled and flagged are answers rather than decisions here.

-- The posted body is not echoed forward. This node's answer REPLACES the item the
-- trigger was handed, which is what run_id travels for on ar-ingest's twin, but a
-- capture body IS the payload and copying it onto every item below would carry the
-- whole capture through the pass. The node that stores it reads it back off
-- $('Capture Webhook').first().json.body, which is the handle every node here has on
-- the request.

-- Every list is ordered, which nothing downstream requires and every reader benefits
-- from: two captures against one unchanged domain hand the nodes below the same lists
-- in the same order, so a diff between two passes is about the captures rather than
-- about the order a planner happened to return rows in.
SELECT
  (SELECT source_id FROM claim) AS source_id,
  (SELECT domain_id FROM source) AS domain_id,

  -- The source row, cut to the members the groups below read. It is also the
  -- resolution path: domain_id comes off it, so every list beneath is scoped by a
  -- column of this row rather than by anything the envelope said. parser_config and
  -- contract are what the extraction reads, the two stamps and the counter are what
  -- source-health.ts turns into a verdict, and kind and endpoint travel because a
  -- reader holding one of these rows should not have to go and fetch what it is.
  (SELECT to_jsonb(s) FROM source s) AS source,

  -- The domain row, cut to the members the nodes below read. feature_version is the
  -- one that has to travel: a document written on this path is read against the same
  -- pin ar-ingest writes, and fetching one integer separately is the lookup node this
  -- shape exists to avoid. NULL rather than an empty object when nothing resolved,
  -- which is the same discriminator domain_id carries.
  (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
     'id', d.id,
     'slug', d.slug,
     'name', d.name,
     'settings', d.settings,
     'feature_version', d.feature_version,
     'embedding_model', d.embedding_model)
     FROM domains d
    WHERE d.id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)) AS domain,

  -- The personas. system_text is operator-owned prose and is the trusted half of what
  -- prompt-frame.ts composes around an untrusted chunk. No node on this canvas makes
  -- a model call, so nothing here reads them today; they are selected because the
  -- design fixes personas and taxonomy as what this node fetches, and because a
  -- capture that grows a judging step should not grow a second lookup with it.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', p.id,
       'role', p.role,
       'system_text', p.system_text)
       ORDER BY p.role, p.id)
       FROM personas p
      WHERE p.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS personas,

  -- The categories, which are the buckets the terms below are filed under. key rather
  -- than id is what a reader downstream matches on: features.ts builds a column name
  -- out of it and static-gate.ts groups hits by it, so the surrogate id travels for
  -- an operator's benefit and the key is what the libraries read.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'key', c.key,
       'name', c.name,
       'parent_id', c.parent_id)
       ORDER BY c.key, c.id)
       FROM categories c
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS categories,

  -- The terms, joined to their category's key rather than carrying category_id. Four
  -- members and this exact spelling, because three libraries read this one list and
  -- each reads a different subset of it: static-gate.ts takes pattern, weight and
  -- polarity, features.ts takes pattern and category, and feature-version.ts takes
  -- all four. A term list selected without the join satisfies the first reader and
  -- starves the other two, with nothing failing.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'category', c.key,
       'pattern', t.pattern,
       'weight', t.weight,
       'polarity', t.polarity)
       ORDER BY c.key, t.pattern, t.id)
       FROM terms t
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = t.category_id
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS terms,

  -- The criteria, joined to their category the same way. Nothing on this canvas reads
  -- them: they are ar-score's subject, and the group that closes this pass hands that
  -- workflow the findings to score rather than this context, so it fetches its own.
  -- They are selected here because the taxonomy is these three tables, and a node
  -- group added below reads them without a second lookup.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', k.id,
       'category', c.key,
       'value', k.value,
       'kind', k.kind)
       ORDER BY c.key, k.kind, k.id)
       FROM criteria k
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = k.category_id
      WHERE k.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS criteria

WITH
-- The first thing this canvas does with the request, and it does it before anything
-- has judged the request. No member of the body has been read except the source id
-- the node above took out of it, and this statement writes the whole of it into
-- documents.raw with a parse_status of failed. Nothing below re-runs the write: the
-- group that reads the envelope, and the group that extracts under it, both act on
-- the row this statement left.

-- That ordering is the point rather than a convenience. A push source cannot be
-- re-read. A feed that answered something unusable is fetched again on the next pass,
-- so a refusal there costs one cycle; a capture refused before it was stored is gone,
-- and whoever posted it has already moved on. src/lib/capture-contract.ts states the
-- same rule from the other side, and every sentence it returns lands in
-- documents.parse_error on a row that already exists.

-- Three parameters, in declaration order: the domain the claimed source resolved to,
-- the source id the envelope claimed, and the request body as one jsonb. The body
-- binds as one value rather than as several because none of its members has been
-- judged, and a capture body is a bare string or a list as readily as an object.
-- JSON.stringify makes valid jsonb of all three, and the nullif is what puts a
-- request carrying no body back to SQL NULL rather than the JSON null literal.
posted AS (
  SELECT
    $1::bigint AS domain_id,
    $2::bigint AS source_id,
    nullif($3::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS raw
),

-- The key this row stands on until the extraction below produces the real one.
-- documents.hash is NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and the digest that column eventually
-- carries is over a url and a body, neither of which has been read yet. So the row is
-- keyed provisionally, on the posted body as jsonb renders it, under a prefix no
-- content digest can hold: a content digest is 64 hexadecimal characters, and the
-- colon is the whole of the guarantee.

-- jsonb rather than the bytes as they arrived, deliberately. Two requests differing
-- only in the order of their keys or in their whitespace are one capture, and jsonb
-- renders both the same way, so the key collapses them into one row.

-- What that collapse covers is a second POST arriving before the first has been
-- promoted. It is not the repeat-capture guard, which is documents.hash's own job and
-- happens one group below under the content digest: by then the standing row carries
-- that digest, and a second POST of the same envelope conflicts with nothing here.
-- Both windows are covered and neither loses a payload. A row still carrying this
-- prefix is one whose pass stopped before the boundary, and re-POSTing the capture
-- lands on that row and finishes it.

-- Two conditions are what confine this statement to captures there is somewhere to
-- put. documents.domain_id is NOT NULL, so an envelope naming a source this
-- deployment does not hold has no corpus to be written to, which is the reading Load
-- Domain Context answers and leaves to this group. A request carrying no body at all
-- has nothing to store, and a row recording it would say a document was captured when
-- what happened was that somebody reached the endpoint. Neither is dropped in
-- silence: the outer SELECT still answers its one item, with no document id and a
-- sentence saying which of the two it was.
candidate AS (
  SELECT
    p.domain_id,
    p.source_id,
    p.raw,
    'pending-capture:'
      || encode(sha256(convert_to(p.raw::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') AS hash
  FROM posted p
  WHERE p.domain_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p.raw IS NOT NULL
),

-- The write. parse_status is written rather than left to its default, and what it is
-- written to is failed. The column defaults to ok and its own comment says what that
-- default cannot tell apart; here the honest answer is neither of those. Nothing has
-- read this payload, so ok would be a claim no writer on this path can make, and a
-- failure carrying its reason is the state the row is actually in until the boundary
-- below says otherwise.

-- parse_error is a constant sentence and carries nothing off the request. The no-echo
-- rule capture-contract.ts states is total on this path, and the reason is sharper
-- here than anywhere else on these canvases: this text is written from a body no
-- boundary has judged, so a template with a hole in it would put a stranger's value
-- into a column an operator reads. The whole body is in raw beside it, which is where
-- a value belongs.

-- url is NULL and body is the empty string, and both are placeholders the extraction
-- below writes over. documents.body is NOT NULL and may still be empty, which its own
-- comment argues at length: an empty body is a capture that yielded no text and was
-- kept anyway. Here it is a capture nothing has tried to read yet.

-- captured_at is left to its default, which is now. That column is when the pipeline
-- captured the document, and for a push that is the moment this row was written. The
-- client's own capturedAt is a claim inside an envelope nothing has judged, so it
-- stays in raw, and once the boundary has accepted it, it travels into the provenance
-- note src/sources/push-capture.ts records.

-- DO NOTHING is what makes the collapse above write no second row, and the conflict
-- target is the constraint by NAME rather than the column list, so renaming the
-- constraint breaks this statement instead of quietly arbitrating on something else.
written AS (
  INSERT INTO documents (
    domain_id, source_id, hash, url, body, raw, parse_status, parse_error)
  SELECT
    c.domain_id,
    c.source_id,
    c.hash,
    NULL::text,
    '',
    c.raw,
    'failed',
    'the capture was stored before validation and nothing has judged it since'
  FROM candidate c
  ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT documents_hash_unique DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT
-- ONE ROW OUT, whatever happened. The insert sits in a CTE and this SELECT names no
-- FROM, so the node answers exactly one item for the one item it was handed. A
-- capture that was stored, a second POST that wrote nothing, and a request there was
-- no row to write each answer one item, and every group below reads a document id
-- rather than counting what reached it.

-- document_id is the row this capture is in, whether or not this pass is what put it
-- there. COALESCE reads it out of the insert when there was one and out of the corpus
-- when there was not, and only one of the two can ever answer: this query reads the
-- snapshot the statement began under, so it cannot see the row the CTE just wrote.
-- NULL means there is no row at all, which is one of the two refusals above.

-- document_stored is the other half of that pair and answers a different question. A
-- second POST of a capture already standing is a request that worked and wrote
-- nothing, so a reader counting new material reads this flag while a reader following
-- a document reads the id, and neither has to infer its answer from the other.

-- store_error says which refusal it was, and it is a constant either way. It is not
-- documents.parse_error and must not be read as one: that column is about a payload
-- that was stored and not read, where this is about a request there was nowhere to
-- store. The group below refuses the capture on it, and the group that closes the
-- pass records it.

-- The branches are read body first, and the order is the whole of what an operator is
-- told. Load Domain Context takes the source id out of the posted body, so a request
-- carrying no body always resolves no source as well: read the other way round, every
-- bodyless request would be reported as one naming a source this deployment does not
-- hold, which is a sentence about a claim nobody made. The narrower reason is the
-- true one, and it goes first.

-- The context is not echoed forward. This node's answer REPLACES Load Domain
-- Context's, and the source row, the domain row and the taxonomy are read back off
-- $('Load Domain Context').first().json by whichever node needs them. One request is
-- one item here, so a name is a safer handle than a copy able to disagree with the
-- row it was taken from.
  (SELECT domain_id FROM posted) AS domain_id,
  (SELECT source_id FROM posted) AS source_id,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT w.id FROM written w),
    (SELECT d.id FROM documents d JOIN candidate c ON c.hash = d.hash))
    AS document_id,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM written) AS document_stored,
  CASE
    WHEN (SELECT raw FROM posted) IS NULL
    THEN 'the request carried no body to store'
    WHEN (SELECT domain_id FROM posted) IS NULL
    THEN 'the request named no source row this deployment holds'
  END AS store_error

parameters.content:
## Posted, Not Scheduled

This workflow starts when something outside this system POSTs to it, and the Webhook node on this canvas is the whole of what makes that possible. It holds no clock and may not acquire one: `ar-dispatch` carries the only Schedule Trigger in the system, and `tests/invariants/workflows.test.ts` counts them across every built workflow and names the one file allowed to hold one.

It is also the first workflow here that ARMS. `ar-ingest` is reached through an Execute Workflow node, and activating a workflow whose only trigger is that one registers nothing at all; a webhook registers a URL. `scripts/activate-workflows.sh` reads that split off each built artifact rather than off a list kept beside it, which is what lets this file change its answer without an edit anywhere else.

### What arrives, and what has judged it

One item per request, carrying `headers`, `params`, `query` and `body` among others. `body` is the capture envelope, and NOTHING has looked at it: `capture-contract.ts` runs below, after the raw body has been stored, which is the ordering that makes a refused capture a stored failure instead of a lost one. So the first node to read anything off the envelope is `Load Domain Context`, and all it reads is the source the envelope claims.

That read happens in SQL rather than in the expression beside it. The whole body binds as one jsonb parameter, the source id is taken out of it under a bounded digit pattern, and both the pattern and what it refuses are commented at the statement. An expression can import nothing and is read by no gate here, so a rule with any shape to it belongs where a comment can explain it.

### The boundary is the contract, not the caller

What this canvas judges is SHAPE: the envelope against `capture-contract.ts`, and the claimed source id against the `sources` table. Neither of those asks WHO posted, and the Webhook node declares `authentication` as `none`. Arming this workflow therefore publishes a path that writes rows, and whatever fronts the instance is the whole of what stands between that path and anybody who can reach it. `docs/architecture/04-sources.md` is where the contract a client writes to is documented.

## Stored Before Anything Reads It

`Store Raw Capture` writes the request body into `documents.raw` with a `parse_status` of `failed`, and it runs before any node has judged what arrived. The ordering is the whole of this group. It is not a first draft of the write the boundary below would rather make, and it is not a place a pass comes back to.

A push source cannot be re-read. A feed that answered something unusable is fetched again on the next pass, so a refusal there costs one cycle. A capture refused before it was stored is gone, and whoever posted it has already moved on. `src/lib/capture-contract.ts` states the same rule from the other side: every sentence it returns lands in `documents.parse_error` on a row that already exists.

### A later step upgrades the status

Nothing re-runs this write. The group below reads the envelope, and the group after it promotes the row it finds: `parse_status` becomes `ok`, and the `hash`, `url` and `body` the extraction produced are written over the placeholders left here. A refused envelope leaves the row where it is, carrying the boundary's own sentence in `parse_error` and the whole body in `raw` beside it. Either way it is the same row, moved on rather than written again.

So a row still carrying `failed` and this node's own sentence says something exact: that pass stopped between the store and the boundary. That is the one state this ordering exists to make visible, and it is a row an operator can read, replay against a corrected config, and promote.

### The key is provisional

`documents.hash` is NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and the digest that column eventually carries is over a url and a body neither of which has been extracted yet. So the row is keyed on the posted body under a prefix no content digest can hold, and the promotion replaces it. Recognising a genuine repeat capture is `documents.hash`'s own job and happens there, under the content digest; what the provisional key collapses is a second POST arriving before the first was promoted.

### Two requests have nowhere to be stored

`documents.domain_id` is NOT NULL, so an envelope naming a source this deployment does not hold has no corpus to be written to. A request carrying no body has nothing to store at all. Neither is dropped in silence: the node answers its one item with no document id and a constant sentence saying which, and the groups below refuse the capture on it.
